source.title: Reducing Logprob Without Causal Verification: Diagnosing SAE-Based PII Suppression in LLMs
source.authors: Chaerin Lee; Wonho Lee; Sohee Park; Daeseon Choi

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies SAE-based PII suppression and evaluates intervention selectivity. It reports SAE reconstruction-quality measurements, but does not test whether SAE reconstruction errors are linearly predictable, how error norms scale across SAE sizes, or any other listed version of the dark-matter claim.
record.gate_note: Table 5 reports reconstruction quality by model and layer (relative error over all token positions, relative error at PII positions, and cosine similarity at PII positions). These measurements do not test the error-structure or SAE-size claims. The paper's other intervention and causal-mediation results concern PII suppression, not dark matter.
record.test_reason: The paper studies SAE-feature interventions for PII suppression against random-direction controls. Its only SAE-error data are reconstruction-quality figures for nine model-layer SAEs (Table 5). These are all one size (×8, k=32), with no linear prediction of the error, no comparison across SAE sizes, no splice-in loss against random errors, and no comparison of analyses with versus without the error term. The hidden-space intervention keeps the error term by design. The authors say the selectivity ratio is invariant to it but do not measure that. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that logprob reduction cannot distinguish feature-specific PII suppression from magnitude artifacts: 17/36 cells pass on logprob alone versus 1/36 under multi-metric criteria. A causal mediation feasibility study shows that correlation-selected features are mostly indistinguishable from random (97.3%). They call for causally grounded candidate generation through circuit localization and mediation analysis. They draw no conclusion about SAE error structure.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses task-specific top-k SAEs for PII-suppression interventions; it does not implement or evaluate the dark-matter method or claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction quality varies by model and layer; the paper notes higher PII-position relative error in the deeper Llama layer 24 and Qwen layer 27.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5: relative reconstruction error at PII token positions is much higher in deep layers (Llama L24 39.20%, Qwen L27 35.59%) than over all tokens (10.45%, 11.28%). Elsewhere it is low (about 2-9%), apart from Llama L16 at 13.53%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error is concentrated on specific token types (here PII tokens) in some deep layers, despite high corpus-level variance explained.

record.problems: For the reconstruction-quality measurements relevant here, the paper reports only nine model-layer configurations and does not compare SAE sizes or test the structure of the residual error. The paper itself says it does not test larger expansion factors such as ×16 or ×32, alternative sparsity levels, or different SAE objectives.

untested.parts: Whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation; not examined.
Error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and persistence with scale. Only one SAE size is trained, and the authors explicitly do not ablate ×16 or ×32.
Loss from splicing in the reconstruction versus random errors of the same norm; not measured.
Linear versus nonlinear error components and their learnability; not examined.
Whether feature-based analyses lose behaviour without the error term. The error term is kept and the z-space comparison is left to future work.
Whether dark matter shrinks with other architectures, sparsity levels or objectives. The authors explicitly do not vary these.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are SAE quality diagnostics, correctly linked to no version. The paper does not cite the dark-matter original. Its handling of the error term (kept in hidden-space steering; selectivity ratio claimed invariant) is a design choice, not a test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error vanishes with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than equal-size random errors.
Whether linear and nonlinear error components correspond to distinct kinds of dark matter or differ in learnability.
Whether analyses based on SAE features lose model behavior unless the SAE error term is retained.
Whether SAE training choices cause dark matter or whether it shrinks under alternative architectures or end-to-end training.
